rows.title: Arkin's Castle
rows.evidence: Arkin's Castle (Irish: Caisleán Aircín) is a 13th-century ruined castle on the island of Inishmore, County Galway, Ireland.
rows.summary: Arkin's Castle (Irish: Caisleán Aircín) is a 13th-century ruined castle on the island of Inishmore, County Galway, Ireland. It is owned by the Department of Climate, Energy and the Environment of Ireland.

rows.title: Eilean Dearg Castle
rows.evidence: The island was once home to a castle, which was destroyed by naval action in Argyll's Rising in 1685.
rows.summary: Eilean Dearg is a small island in Loch Ruel (or Loch Riddon) in Argyll, Scotland. The island was once home to a castle, which was destroyed by naval action in Argyll's Rising in 1685. No visible remains of the castle are to be found, but archaeologists excavated the site between 1964 and 1967, finding the castle's hall, chapel, a tower and the foundations of the wall, along with a gate.

rows.title: Caisteal Bheagram
rows.evidence: Ranald Bane, or his heirs, built Casteal Bheagram, on Loch an Eilean in Skirhough, as their local stronghold.
rows.summary: Ranald Bane, or his heirs, built Casteal Bheagram, on Loch an Eilean in Skirhough, as their local stronghold. Skirhough is a district of South Uist, named after its main settlement, Howmore. Caisteal Bheagram, as a small tower, was more useful merely as a refuge. The South Uist article captions the ruin Caisteal Bheagram in Drimsdale.

rows.title: Castle on Tory Island
rows.evidence: The rebels took shelter in the castle on the island but it became obvious they could not hold out for long.
rows.summary: Survivors of O'Doherty's rebellion withdrew to Tory Island, pursued there by Sir Henry Folliott, the Governor of Ballyshannon. The rebels took shelter in the castle on the island but it became obvious they could not hold out for long. The Constable of the castle, Sir Mulmory McSweeney, began to kill his fellow defenders in hopes of securing a pardon.
